Ferdinand: Miranda? How is life in Boston?
Miranda: Unexpectedly busy. Let's catch up on that later. How are things in Brazil?
Ferdinand: Things are going supremely well here. I have successfully connected with some associates in Colombia too.
Miranda: Great. Now, to change the subject, I'm holding a meeting this week to discuss our PR event. Oh, that reminds me, do you have access to a webcam?
Ferdinand: Hold on to that question ... have you got an event date yet? I have an idea ...

Miranda: What's that?
Ferdinand: Sao Paulo Fashion Week is just around the corner. Let's host the events simultaneously! We could have a big screen to broadcast the events.
Miranda: Ferdinand, I believe you're charmed. Hope your good luck will quickly head north. Getting back to your schedule ...
Ferdinand: Thursday afternoon is my only opening this week.
Miranda: I'll schedule the meeting then.

Ferdinand: Thanks. Oh, before I forget, what bad news do you keep repeatedly hinting at?
Miranda: Only a leak over social media about massive layoffs at Holly's.
Ferdinand: What? A layoff leak? What's going on?
Miranda: Farmani is trying hard to cut expenses wherever he can. But don't worry. Janet's carefully designing a plan. It will turn things around.
Ferdinand: I'm awfully glad to hear that. I will be in touch Thursday then!

Adverbs are words that are used mainly to modify verbs and tell us the way in which something happens.
Adverbs of manner, however, are used primarily to tell us how something happens.

1. Adverbs of manner are usually placed either after the main verb or after the object.
    • She has carefully designed a new plan for the company.
    • He is trying hard to cut expenses.
    • I am hoping that things will quickly head north. (or head north quickly)

1. Adverbs of manner can be added to a verb to modify its meaning. Compare the following:
    • I have connected with some of our associates.
    vs.
    • I have successfully connected with some of our associates.

1. Adverbs of manner can not be put between a verb and its direct object.
    • I think we should host simultaneously the events.
    • I think we should host the events simultaneously.
Expressions for Changing Topics in Oral Conversations

When speaking a foreign language, especially English, it is important that you acquire a set of conversation strategies which will help you deal with the spontaneity of spoken English. A very important strategy you need to master is changing topics in a conversation. Here are a few expressions you can use to change the subject of a conversation.

• Let's catch up on that later / tomorrow / in a few hours.
  • Now, to change the subject ...
  • Oh, that reminds me ...
  • Hold on to that question / thought / idea, but ...
  • Oh, before I forget, ...

A: So, how's the new position?
B: Busy, but let's catch up on that later. Tell me about your new job.

A: I'm holding a meeting next week to ...
B: Oh, before I forget ... next week's meeting has been cancelled.
A: Now to change the subject, have you contacted the office regarding the details for the party?
to communicate with someone using a telephone or computer network
Example: I have successfully connected with some associates in Colombia.
These are words you use when you are planning an event in the workplace.
gathering people to discuss things and make decisions
Example: I'm holding a meeting this week to discuss our events.
having the opportunity or means to use something
Example: Do you have access to a webcam?
to reduce the amount of money you spend on something
Example: The boss is trying hard to cut expenses.
to organize and be in charge of a party or event
Example: We are going to host both events.
happening or done at the same time
Example: Let's host the events simultaneously.
to send out a programme or event to be received by radios or televisions
Example: We could have a screen to broadcast the events.
to go in a particular direction
Example: Hope your good luck will quickly head north.
